checks.assessment: Session acquisition, health mutation/deadline and SQL failures remain real typed CacheError/CronError paths with source chaining. bounded_session_error retains CacheError as source; schedule_store_failed retains CronError. Management returns through the existing blocking helper and error mapping; guard drop occurs on success/error/unwind. No new opaque public error-only string boundary identified.

Instant and Duration preserve monotonic deadlines and units. ScheduleShutdownControl and ScheduleManagementCall carry meaningful policy/ownership. The private usize identities are derived from live Shared/deadline Arc allocations, never supplied by callers; control clones retain the deadline allocation. No repeated raw identity validation or unit confusion warrants another public newtype.

Arc<Mutex<Option<Instant>>> is justified because shutdown updates must be visible inside already-running blocking operations. Critical sections only copy/shorten/reset the deadline; SQLite/mutex waits occur outside this controller lock. RefCell stacks are thread-local dynamic call context and never cross await. The management guard is !Send/!Sync via PhantomData<Rc<()>>, keys both exact control and physical Shared identity, and removes its registration on Drop. Worker scopes and HealthSession restore their stacks and SQLite settings while the connection mutex is still held. Separate restore setters execute independently on error.

Controller setup, deadline shortening/reset, exemption creation and policy checks return direct values where infallible. Session/store/management Result boundaries represent actual mutex-budget, SQL, read-only, validation or join failure. No new Result-only-Ok ceremony is needed; CanonicalLog::emit returns Result because the upstream trait requires it, not a locally invented fake failure boundary.

lifecycle_source_checks: cron.rs:200-251 fixes grace and cleanup deadlines from the same stop boundary. It installs worker deadline at grace, selects expiry/hurry separately from the pinned shutdown future, requests kill and callback before awaiting the same real worker future, only shortens finish_by on hurry, resets control after the real worker join, and awaits bounded cache idle cleanup. No newly detached timeout/worker abort or second Scheduler was introduced.

Published sc-cron-0.1.1 scheduler.rs:904-931 explicitly awaits its owned worker after timeout; worker.rs:539-550 awaits actual spawn_blocking store completion. The consumer adapter cooperates with those semantics. It does not claim arbitrary third-party stores/native code are preemptible.

health.rs:194-215 checks a live controller during mutex acquisition; :141-173 checks it during busy retry; :256-270 checks it during SQLite progress. schedule.rs:255-281 checks decoding. Health deadline and read-only checks are separate and remain effective inside management exemptions.

schedule.rs:643-652 creates a view over the existing Shared connection. manage():714-721 uses Scheduler::share and inline documented public management operations on the owned blocking thread, preserving the same Core immediate notification. Run-due and job callbacks receive no management exemption.

Source tests cover same view versus other view/connection, error/unwind restoration, real held mutex/BEGIN IMMEDIATE/recursive SQL contention, ordinary/hurried/zero stop, reuse, same-Scheduler cancellation and rejected concurrent start. Observed independent clean-path test log has the corresponding passing tests. This source review does not certify test cleanup boundedness or replace the flaky-test owner.
